correctness.rationale: Uniquely determined alternating sink-removal layers give an exact last-block exponential generating function, whose finite coefficients match exhaustive DAG enumerations in 15 graphs and the known Stirling total in 81 size pairs. For each fixed sink multiplicity the numerator is entire and strictly positive at the established smooth minimal saddle for \(1-(e^x-1)(e^y-1)\); all marked and unmarked numerators share the denominator. The published uniform ACSV transfer gives exact limiting ratios, which sum to total mass one, establishing total variation. The strict-mixture and direction-of-imbalance statements then follow from the parameter equations; no computational extrapolation is used for the limit.

originality.rationale: The novel claim is the *unequal-density joint sink-side/number distribution*, with distinct zero-truncated Poisson components and side weights. The 2014 graph-count paper and 2019 unmarked bivariate ACSV result supply the combinatorial and analytic foundation but not the marked numerator. The 2019 general sink polynomial of Hwang et al. provides graph-wide exact sink counts but not this specialized asymptotic classification. The 2020 unique-sink enumeration does not imply an all-multiplicities joint limit by itself; 2024 work studies longest paths. A previously published equal-density sink law is explicitly credited and not recast as new. Both indexed and primary-text comparisons found no explicit unequal-density result, subject to remaining historical-priority limitations.
residual_risks: The full text of West (1995) was not inspected; unreported marked enumerations in older literature may alter historical priority.
The 2019 transfer theorem makes the limit relatively accessible once the final-block marking is supplied. Independent priority judgment is still needed.
The equal-side 2026 indexed result was examined as a public summary, not as a full-text negative comparison.
Other general sink enumerators may contain a non-obvious equivalent after specialization; no uniqueness guarantee is claimed.

value.rationale: The complete sink-side and sink-number joint law is a natural statistic of task-termination structure in random acyclic bipartite dependency graphs, and of the final block of lonesum matrices. In the unequally sized limit it is genuinely a mixture of two distinct zero-truncated Poisson laws and systematically favors the larger class; the balanced case conceals both effects. This distinguishes a mathematically motivated new probability-law classification from mere recomputation of total orientation counts or the existing single-sink slice.
